Printcart Store – Full Web-to-Print Solution for WordPress

Printcart Store is a web-to-print product designer for WooCommerce that lets customers personalize products online and automatically generates high-resolution, print-ready files (PDF, SVG, PNG, JPG CMYK) — with built-in AI print tools, a B2B store module, global template collections, and print-on-demand automation.

Turn your WooCommerce store into a full web-to-print & print-on-demand business.

  • Enable customers to design & customize any product
  • Generate print-ready files (PDF, SVG, PNG, JPG CMYK)
  • AI print tools — Preflight quality check, Background Removal & Image Upscale
  • B2B & B2C store — customer tiers, pricing rules, bulk quotes & brand assets
  • Global template collections — ready-made designs from Printcart
  • Seamless WooCommerce integration — no coding required
  • 100% mobile-friendly customizer — works on any device
  • Cloud Print API for full Web-to-Print automation
  • Enterprise: Printcart Dashboard + API to manage & scale multiple WordPress stores (enterprise only)

Live Demo & Landing Page

See more on the Printcart YouTube channel.

What is Printcart Store? A Web-to-Print Product Designer for WooCommerce

Printcart Store is the ultimate print-on-demand (POD) and Web2Print solution that enables your customers to customize products online, generate high-resolution print files, and streamline order fulfillment.

Perfect for selling:

  • T-shirts, hoodies, and apparel
  • Mugs, bottles, and drinkware
  • Business cards, flyers, and brochures
  • Posters, banners, and signage
  • Stickers, labels, and decals
  • Phone cases, pillows, and home decor
  • Customized packaging & more

Power your printshop with a complete Web-to-Print system.

AI Print Tools

Once a Printcart store is connected, an AI toolset runs directly on your order and design files, metered by your Printcart AI tokens:

  • AI Preflight — checks the print PDF for resolution, bleed and color before it goes to production
  • AI Background Removal — removes the background from an uploaded image
  • AI Image Upscale — increases image resolution for large-format print

The tools run from the Order detail and Design File screens. When your token balance runs low, the plugin shows a clear prompt with a link to top up on the Printcart dashboard.

B2B & B2C Store Workflow

An optional module for corporate and wholesale selling — off by default, enabled under WooCommerce → Printcart → Set Up → Tools.

  • Company store management, customer tiers and pricing rules
  • Team workspaces and invitations
  • Bulk Quotes — a custom quote workflow with a front-end B2B portal
  • Brand Templates and Brand Media — manage each store’s approved design templates and brand assets (logos, images) in one place

Global Template Collections

Give customers a head start with ready-made design collections curated by Printcart. Browse the global template library, assign a template to any product, and let buyers customize it in the designer — no need to build every design from scratch.

Enterprise — Scale Multiple WordPress Stores

For agencies and multi-brand operations, the Printcart Dashboard and its API let you manage and scale many WordPress / WooCommerce stores from one place — centralized licensing, cloud storage, and product/order sync and automation across all your sites. Available on the enterprise plan.

Printcart is designed for print businesses, eCommerce store owners, and creative entrepreneurs who want to offer customizable products online — from print-on-demand stores and marketing agencies to full-scale printshops.

Key Features & Benefits

For Store Owners & Printshops

  • Seamless WooCommerce integration — works with all themes & product types
  • Sell print-on-demand products — no inventory required
  • Cloud Print API integration — automate order fulfillment & printing
  • Multi-product support — T-shirts, mugs, business cards, etc.
  • Dynamic pricing matrix — charge based on product type, color, and size
  • Product design previews — offer real-time customer previews
  • Custom order upload — allow customers to upload designs
  • SVG, PDF & PNG print-ready files — perfect for print production
  • Multi-vendor compatible — works with Dokan, WC Vendors, WCFM

For Customers & Buyers

  • User-friendly drag & drop designer — no design skills needed
  • Customize with text, images & cliparts — 1.5M+ free cliparts & fonts
  • QR code generator — let customers add QR codes to products
  • Advanced typography — 600+ Google Fonts & curved text options
  • Social sharing — customers can share their designs on Facebook, Twitter, etc.
  • Instant product previews — see designs before ordering
  • Order management dashboard — customers can edit and re-order designs

How It Works — Admin & Buyer Workflow

Step 1: Store setup & product configuration (admin panel)

  • Install & activate the Printcart Store plugin (download here)
  • Configure your custom design zones for each product
  • Set up pricing rules & print-ready file formats (PDF, SVG, PNG, JPG)
  • Enable Cloud Print API for order automation

Step 2: Customer experience & customization

  • Customers visit your WooCommerce store & select a product
  • Use the drag & drop designer to customize text, images & colors
  • Preview & finalize the design
  • Add to cart & checkout

Step 3: Order processing & fulfillment

  • Admin receives a high-resolution print-ready file (PDF, SVG, PNG)
  • Orders sync with Printcart Cloud API for automated printing
  • Customers receive real-time tracking updates

External services

The designer and WooCommerce data remain on your site until you use a cloud feature. Print-ready PDF generation is cloud-only; it calls Printcart services over HTTPS when a PDF or PDF preview is requested. Other connected features call the Printcart cloud API only when you use them:

  • Store connection: your credentials (Sid / Secret / Unauth Token), site URL and the WooCommerce REST keys generated for the connection are sent so Printcart can register the store and sync products/orders. Credentials can live in wp-config.php and are never printed to the page, JavaScript or logs.
  • Print-ready PDF rendering (api.cloud2print.net): the public URLs of saved design assets plus product dimensions, fonts and production settings are sent when an administrator, customer or background order workflow requests a PDF.
  • PDF preview/image conversion (pdf2image.cloud2print.net, with pdf2img.cloud2print.net as a fallback): the generated PDF URL, requested DPI, image format and ICC profile identifier are sent when a PDF preview or image export is requested.
  • AI tools (Background Removal, Image Upscale, Preflight): the selected image or PDF URL — plus print specifications for Preflight — is sent for processing and the result is returned to your uploads folder.
  • Token wallet: balance, packages and top-up session; top-ups are completed on the Printcart dashboard.
  • Order sync (on by default once a store is connected; turn it off under WooCommerce > Printcart > Printcart Account > Order sync): when an order is paid, and on every later status change, the order number, status, totals, currency, payment method title, the customer’s name, email, phone and company, the billing and shipping addresses, the line items (product IDs, SKU, name, quantity, price) and the public URLs of the order’s print PDFs are sent to api.printcart.com so the order appears in the Printcart Dashboard for production. Orders placed in the last 30 days (configurable) are sent once when the store is first connected.
  • Activation emails: after you connect a store, the plugin notifies api.printcart.com that the store is connected (and later, if no product has the design tool enabled) so Printcart can email you a secure link to your dashboard and setup steps. Only the event name, the plugin version and simple counts are sent. No customer data is included.
  • Setup and upgrade events: once a store is connected, the plugin sends anonymous setup and upgrade events (for example: setup wizard started, connect failed, upgrade clicked, product limit reached) with the screen name and simple counts, so Printcart can improve setup. Events that happen before connecting are kept on the site and sent only after you connect. No customer data is included.
  • Customer file uploads (connected stores only): after a customer uploads a design file, the plugin asks for their name, email, optional phone and a note, and sends them with the product, quantity and the public URLs of the uploaded files to api.printcart.com. Printcart records a pending order, emails the store owner and sends the customer a receipt. The file is added to the cart only after the customer sends these details (or if Printcart cannot be reached).
  • Automatic setup: when you choose “Create account & store automatically”, your name, email, store name and shop URL are sent to api.printcart.com to create the account and store, and Printcart emails you a link to set your Dashboard password.

Printcart is a third-party service, independent of WordPress.org. By connecting a store and using these features you agree to Printcart’s terms and privacy policy:

  • Terms of Service: https://www.printcart.com/en/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://www.printcart.com/en/privacy

Each Printcart plugin is a complete solution for one product niche. One store runs one Printcart solution. To run several Printcart solutions on one store, see Printcart Connect (integration service, Printcart Advanced plan or above).

Once a store is connected, the plugin also tells Printcart which Printcart plugins and versions are active on your site (for example Printcart Store and PC Canvas), so the Printcart Dashboard can show them. Nothing is sent before you connect a store. The connection itself is shared with other Printcart plugins through a small library bundled in each of them (Printcart Connect): connecting once connects them all, and uninstalling one plugin keeps the connection while another Printcart plugin remains.
sections.faq:
Is Printcart Store free?

Yes. A free version is available on WordPress.org. A premium Printcart subscription unlocks cloud processing, the AI print tools, cloud file storage, and full API automation.

What file formats does Printcart Store export?

Every order produces high-resolution, print-ready files — PDF, SVG, PNG and JPG (CMYK) — ready to send straight to production.

Which products can customers customize with Printcart Store?

T-shirts and apparel, mugs and drinkware, business cards, flyers, posters, banners, stickers and labels, phone cases, packaging and more.

Is Printcart Store compatible with WooCommerce HPOS and mobile devices?

Yes. Printcart Store is WooCommerce HPOS-compatible, and the product designer is 100% responsive on desktop, tablet and mobile.

My store is behind a proxy or CDN. How do I make the request-a-quote limit use each visitor’s real IP?

Return the visitor IP that your trusted proxy reports (for example $_SERVER['HTTP_CF_CONNECTING_IP'] on Cloudflare) from the nbdq_raq_rate_limit_ip filter; otherwise every visitor shares one request-a-quote limit.

Printcart is available for WooCommerce, Wix, and Shopify, but the WordPress version is best for businesses that want:

  • Flexible customization — WooCommerce allows custom development for advanced features.

Yes. While the basic plugin is available, a premium subscription is required for:

Printcart is powered by a cloud-based print-commerce system that includes:

sections.changelog:
2.14.6 (2026, Nov 21)

  • Security: Printing Options save and “Move to Trash”, Template Fields mapping save, product import/export and the settings export now require a nonce (settings export also requires a manager role).
  • Security: B2B quote accept/decline links in quote emails carry a signed per-quote token; old links ask for one confirmation click.
  • Security: the setup wizard verifies its nonce and capability; SQL in template and quote lookups is prepared; include paths and file names are validated.
  • Compatibility: PHP 8.4/8.5 deprecations removed (imagedestroy, curl_close, fputcsv arguments); scripts declare version and footer arguments; WooCommerce 11.3 parent-item-key declarations.
  • Code quality: WordPress Plugin Check and WooCommerce QIT warnings cleared (input unslashing/sanitizing, debug output removed, composer.json shipped).
  • Fixed: template gallery paging and filters ran an unprepared query and could return no templates.
  • Changed: the plugin header name now matches the listing name, “Printcart Store – Web to Print Product Designer for WooCommerce”; the full version history moved to changelog.txt.

2.14.5 (2026, Nov 21)

  • Security: the B2B customer list loads users with get_users() and an ID filter only, so no search text ever reaches the user query (WooCommerce.com QIT review).

2.14.4 (2026, Nov 21)

  • Security: the B2B customer list builds its user query from an explicit argument list (login and display-name search columns only, matching by ID), for the WooCommerce.com QIT review.

2.14.3 (2026, Nov 21)

  • Security: the B2B customer list declares its user-query search columns without the e-mail column (WooCommerce.com QIT review).

2.14.2 (2026, Nov 21)

  • Security: the B2B customer search now matches login, e-mail and display name through an escaped, prepared query instead of a WP_User_Query search string; removed a leftover debug method from the printing-options list.
  • Compatibility: explicit htmlspecialchars()/htmlspecialchars_decode() flags for the product guideline and printing tab content (PHP 8.1+), keeping the previous output.

2.14.1 (2026, Nov 21)

  • Security: sanitize and unslash every request value read by the plugin, escape remaining output, and remove the bundled Giphy API key default (merchants add their own key).
  • Compatibility: use the jQuery UI, moment, CodeMirror and React copies that ship with WordPress instead of bundled copies; explicit flags for htmlspecialchars and related functions (PHP 8.1+).
  • Housekeeping: bundled PDF libraries (dompdf, TCPDF, FPDI, TCPDI, EvalMath, JWT) moved to vendor/bundled; translator comments and ordered placeholders for translatable strings; direct-access guards on every PHP file; “Tested up to” kept only in readme.txt.

2.14.0 (2026, Nov 20)

  • Changed: the Printcart Store admin screens now live under WooCommerce > Printcart instead of a separate top-level menu. Every screen keeps its address, and a navigation bar at the top of each screen lists the same sections as before.
  • Changed: the text domain is now printcart-integration, so translations from translate.wordpress.org load. Translation files made for the old domain web-to-print-online-designer are still read for this version.
  • Changed: jQuery UI, AngularJS, Bootstrap, Lodash and jsPDF ship inside the plugin instead of loading from third-party CDNs; jsPDF is pinned to 4.2.1.
  • Security: output escaping and prepared database queries across the admin screens, storefront templates and the B2B module.
  • Tweak: WooCommerce tested up to 11.3.

2.13.6 (2026, Oct 26)

  • Security: files uploaded through the designer, the “Upload design” step and product option fields are now checked by type and content before they are stored; executable files are refused, uploaded SVG artwork is cleaned of scripts, and the upload folders are protected on more servers.
  • Fixed: “Upload design” failed with a server error on products that have no upload settings of their own; the store-wide upload settings now apply there.
  • Fixed: “Process” could fail with a server error when a product’s designer background or overlay was stored as a media ID or the image could not be read; the preview is now made without that image instead.

2.13.5 (2026, Oct 20)

  • Fixed: on stores with PayPal buttons on the product page, a customized design could be missing from the cart after “Process”: the price check of the PayPal buttons ran between saving the design and adding the product, and used up the design link. Price checks of other plugins no longer touch the designs of the real cart.

2.13.4 (2026, Oct 17)

  • Fixed: on stores that cache product pages, a first-time shopper’s customized design could be missing from the cart after the first “Process”; the product was added without its design and a second Process was needed. The designer now starts the cart session itself before the design is saved.

Older versions: see changelog.txt in the plugin folder.

External services

The designer and WooCommerce data remain on your site until you use a cloud feature. Print-ready PDF generation is cloud-only; it calls Printcart services over HTTPS when a PDF or PDF preview is requested. Other connected features call the Printcart cloud API only when you use them:

  • Store connection: your credentials (Sid / Secret / Unauth Token), site URL and the WooCommerce REST keys generated for the connection are sent so Printcart can register the store and sync products/orders. Credentials can live in wp-config.php and are never printed to the page, JavaScript or logs.
  • Print-ready PDF rendering (api.cloud2print.net): the public URLs of saved design assets plus product dimensions, fonts and production settings are sent when an administrator, customer or background order workflow requests a PDF.
  • PDF preview/image conversion (pdf2image.cloud2print.net, with pdf2img.cloud2print.net as a fallback): the generated PDF URL, requested DPI, image format and ICC profile identifier are sent when a PDF preview or image export is requested.
  • AI tools (Background Removal, Image Upscale, Preflight): the selected image or PDF URL — plus print specifications for Preflight — is sent for processing and the result is returned to your uploads folder.
  • Token wallet: balance, packages and top-up session; top-ups are completed on the Printcart dashboard.
  • Order sync (on by default once a store is connected; turn it off under WooCommerce > Printcart > Printcart Account > Order sync): when an order is paid, and on every later status change, the order number, status, totals, currency, payment method title, the customer’s name, email, phone and company, the billing and shipping addresses, the line items (product IDs, SKU, name, quantity, price) and the public URLs of the order’s print PDFs are sent to api.printcart.com so the order appears in the Printcart Dashboard for production. Orders placed in the last 30 days (configurable) are sent once when the store is first connected.
  • Activation emails: after you connect a store, the plugin notifies api.printcart.com that the store is connected (and later, if no product has the design tool enabled) so Printcart can email you a secure link to your dashboard and setup steps. Only the event name, the plugin version and simple counts are sent. No customer data is included.
  • Setup and upgrade events: once a store is connected, the plugin sends anonymous setup and upgrade events (for example: setup wizard started, connect failed, upgrade clicked, product limit reached) with the screen name and simple counts, so Printcart can improve setup. Events that happen before connecting are kept on the site and sent only after you connect. No customer data is included.
  • Customer file uploads (connected stores only): after a customer uploads a design file, the plugin asks for their name, email, optional phone and a note, and sends them with the product, quantity and the public URLs of the uploaded files to api.printcart.com. Printcart records a pending order, emails the store owner and sends the customer a receipt. The file is added to the cart only after the customer sends these details (or if Printcart cannot be reached).
  • Automatic setup: when you choose “Create account & store automatically”, your name, email, store name and shop URL are sent to api.printcart.com to create the account and store, and Printcart emails you a link to set your Dashboard password.

Printcart is a third-party service, independent of WordPress.org. By connecting a store and using these features you agree to Printcart’s terms and privacy policy:

  • Terms of Service: https://www.printcart.com/en/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://www.printcart.com/en/privacy

Each Printcart plugin is a complete solution for one product niche. One store runs one Printcart solution. To run several Printcart solutions on one store, see Printcart Connect (integration service, Printcart Advanced plan or above).

Once a store is connected, the plugin also tells Printcart which Printcart plugins and versions are active on your site (for example Printcart Store and PC Canvas), so the Printcart Dashboard can show them. Nothing is sent before you connect a store. The connection itself is shared with other Printcart plugins through a small library bundled in each of them (Printcart Connect): connecting once connects them all, and uninstalling one plugin keeps the connection while another Printcart plugin remains.
